quotes.text: If you remember nothing else from this, remember that workflows optimize steps while events optimize time.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Condenses the core thesis of the episode into one memorable contrast.

quotes.text: Centralizing all that cross-system logic in one master flow usually doesn't create control. It actually hides fragility.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Challenges the common belief that a single master flow equals control.

quotes.text: You should use workflows for local task execution like sending a notification or updating a single record. Use events and APIs for business logic that needs to move across different systems.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a clear, practical design rule for when to use workflows versus events.

quotes.text: Orchestration should never depend on a single person leaving the company, changing a password, or losing access to a connection that nobody else understands.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why user-owned credentials make automation fragile and identity part of the control plane.

quotes.text: A green run history can still hide a bad business outcome if the signal arrived late, got duplicated or triggered the wrong action downstream.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shows why monitoring flow runs is not the same as monitoring business outcomes.

takeaways: Workflows optimize individual steps, but business events optimize time, so design cross-system logic around named business moments instead of long master flows.
Dataverse business events and custom APIs let subscribers react in parallel to confirmed facts, which gives clearer ownership and smaller, testable handlers.
Start with one latency-sensitive decision path, back managed identities, event catalogs and event-based observability, and retire polling and mega-flows step by step.
hook: Your Power Automate flows run green, yet the business still reacts too slowly. This episode is for Power Platform architects and automation owners who keep piling logic into master flows. Learn why event-first orchestration with Dataverse business events and API connectors cuts decision latency and makes automation easier to govern.
